key_insight: Deep learning PVS segmentation models can look accurate on internal tests yet still fail to generalize or preserve biologically meaningful results in heterogeneous Alzheimer’s disease cohorts.
clinical_relevance: For Alzheimer’s imaging research, model choice and cohort-specific validation matter because segmentation performance alone may not support reliable biomarker inference.
method: Benchmarked 5 open-source nnU-Net-based PVS segmentation models against manual labels.
Tested on 60 multi-site ADNI-3 participants plus 12 external VALDO challenge scans.
Compared voxel-, object-, lesion-wise Dice and checked whether model-derived PVS burden matched known AD biomarker associations.
evidence_signal: ADNI-PVS-Net had the best internal Dice (0.58±0.14) but performed poorly externally (Dice ≤0.11), while other models generalized better (Dice 0.27–0.30) yet sometimes failed to reproduce the PVS-amyloid relationship.
watch_item: Higher Dice did not guarantee valid downstream biology, and some models misclassified up to 32% of white matter hyperintensities as PVS.
paper_title: Examining the Clinical Utility of Deep Learning Models for Perivascular Space Segmentation in Alzheimer's Disease
